title: [27/1/2024] Percentage of employers in various sectors having difficulty in finding staff in 2003 and 2004
prompt: The table below shows the percentage of employers in various sectors having difficulty in finding staff in 2003 and 2004. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table gives information about three types of recruitment challenges that employers in four different fields faced between 2003 and 2004.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, finding skilled workers was the most prevalent issue among recruiters in all fields. In addition, the percentage of employers that had trouble finding skilled and unskilled workers rose, with the exception of those in commerce, while finding technical and managerial staff saw a decrease in prevalence.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: In terms of skilled workers, from 41% to 45% of businesses in the building and services sectors had difficulty doing so in both years. Meanwhile, about 46% of those in manufacturing and commerce reported the same issue in 2003. In the following year, while inability to find skilled workers experienced a rise in prevalence to 51% in the manufacturing sector, the figures for the commerce sector fell to just 41%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: With regard to unskilled labor, in both years, approximately 27% of recruiters in manufacturing struggled to do so, while roughly a fifth of those in building and commerce experienced this problem. However, the service industry experienced a surge in trouble finding unskilled workers, from 20% in 2003 to 29% in 2004.

Finally, all given industries generally found it easier to hire for technical and managerial roles, as only around a tenth of employers in construction could not have suitable candidates in both years, while the remaining sectors saw figures of under 8% during this period.
